extracted.intended_audience: general readers; journalists, advertisers, and community managers interested in Reddit norms and policies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and norms for interacting with, reporting on, and advertising to Reddit communities, and the site-wide moderation/policy constraints that govern acceptable content and behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect community ownership and seek attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists are advised by the site's policies to respect that "reddit's communities belong to their members" and to seek proper attribution for people's contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using Reddit content for reporting, identify and credit contributors appropriately; do not treat community content as anonymous fodder. The page emphasizes that communities consider themselves owned by members, so outside actors should request permission or attribution rather than assuming free reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising etiquette — avoid feeling manipulative
rubrics_metrics.description: Redditors dislike "feeling manipulated by brands" but respond well to "content that begs for intelligent viewers and participants." Advertisers should avoid stealthy self-promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design promotions that 'spark conversations and feedback.' Avoid astroturfing or campaigns presented as organic user content. Examples: Nissan's branded promotion giving free gifts succeeded but drew ridicule when perceived as astroturfing; marketers are warned that self-promotion is frowned upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AMAs carefully and authentically
rubrics_metrics.description: AMAs import norms of honesty and authenticity into a public venue; using AMAs can get attention for public figures but may not be right for every project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach AMAs with transparent, real engagement — treat unexpected or irreverent questions the same as project-specific ones. AMAs are 'high risk' for promotional use; they work when organizers/participants are prepared for candid interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not publish non-public personally-identifying information (doxxing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following incidents of Internet vigilantism, Reddit introduced a strict rule against the online publication of non-public personally-identifying information; those who break the rule are subject to a site-wide ban and possible deletion of content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community members and moderators must prohibit doxxing; journalists and users should avoid sharing private data. The policy is enforced site-wide and is presented as a clear prohibition rather than a guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on sexual content featuring minors / related safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: The site changed policies to explicitly ban 'suggestive or sexual content featuring minors' (historically linked to controversies such as 'jailbait').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators and users must remove and not host content that sexualizes minors. This is a strict content-policy boundary and has been a trigger for past site policy changes and subreddit bans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies against hate-promoting communities and hate speech
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit updated content policy and introduced rules aimed at curbing communities it believed to be 'promoting hate', resulting in mass subreddit bans for policy violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communities promoting racism, antisemitism, or routine hate speech are subject to quarantine or banning. The page cites the 2020 enforcement that removed ~2,000 subreddits and notes continuing debate about free expression versus removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderator discretion within site-wide rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The website grants subreddit moderators discretion in deciding what content is and is not allowed on their subreddits, so long as site-wide rules are not being violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect variation across subreddits; what is allowed in one community may be removed in another. Moderation is decentralized and community-specific rules should be checked before posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brigading, manipulation, and coordinated disruptive practices are prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit is vulnerable to disruptive or manipulative practices such as troll farms, click farms, astroturfing, and brigading; these are generally against site rules (though not always malicious in intent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organized voting or coordinated attacks on external sites or within Reddit can violate policies; historical examples (e.g., 'Mister Splashy Pants') illustrate both harmless pranks and harmful brigading. Administrators may take action when brigading is malicious or disruptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Users are privacy-conscious — expect ad-blocking and proxies
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit's users tend to be more privacy-conscious than on other websites, often using tools like ad-blocking software and proxies, and they dislike feeling manipulated by brands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertisers and third-party developers should assume a privacy-aware audience: transparent, value-adding engagement performs better than intrusive ads; also expect technical barriers (ad-blockers) to advertising reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution about unsourced user content and misinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to decentralized moderation, user anonymity, and lack of fact-checking systems, the platform is highly prone to spreading misinformation and disinformation; readers should exercise caution taking user-created unsourced content as fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particularly in medical contexts, unsourced advice can be dangerous (studies found very few sources cited). Journalists, researchers, and users should verify claims independently before amplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with legal/regulatory obligations (e.g., age verification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit began requiring age verification for certain features to comply with laws such as the UK's Online Safety Act 2023; features subject to age verification include sexually explicit material, encouragement of suicide and eating disorders, and hateful expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform changes to comply with jurisdictional laws can affect accessibility and how content is moderated; community managers and developers should monitor and adapt to legal compliance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of automated moderation false positives
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit's automatic moderation tools (e.g., AutoModerator) can flag innocuous content incorrectly (example: the word 'Luigi' flagged as 'potentially violent' because of a namesake), leading to misattribution of flags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators should review automated flags for context; users and managers must consider that automated systems can have unintended consequences and require tuning and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising tactical recommendations and risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketers are encouraged to create branded content that 'sparks conversations and feedback' and to use AMAs for public figures, but must be aware these tactics can backfire and be perceived as 'high risk.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include branded promotions that succeeded (Nissan free gifts) and those that were ridiculed for astroturfing. Recommended practice: educate clients that irreverent or off-topic audience engagement must be handled authentically and respectfully.
